Mutual Aid Society. In order to make the Society powerful,

support the Society.

cause, coolies should unite and oppose the dismissal.

A delegation of several gangers will call on Mr. Yu at his

TRANSLATION
Notification No.I of the International Settlement Road
Construction Coolies Mutual Aid Association, dated
February ........., 1937.

Unrest due to a decision by the authorities
to reduce staff exists amo□st us, the road construction
coolies. However, through the assistance rendered to us
by Mr. Yu Ka Ching, we shall not be thrown out of work.
The S.M.C. has declared that there has not been a decision
to reduce staff and at the same time announced the following
conditions of labour:-

"Working hours for the winter season will be 8½ hours
a day, and for summer 9 hours a day. The wages for 1st
class coolies are $0.65 per diem. For wet days and
holidays, those who do not work will be given half-pay,
while those who attend for work will be entitled to
their full wages. There will be three holidays for the
Lunar New Year and one for the Dragon Boat Festival; full
wages being paid to the coolies. Those who work on these
holidays will receive double pay."

The coolies are therefore notified to work peacefully
and without disturbance. Hereafter all coolies should be
diligent at their work, do their duty, and not interfere
with the work of others. Those who disobey these
instructions or conduct illegal activities which are
detrimental to the good name of this Association will be
reported to the S.M.C..

译文

国际租界筑路苦力互助协会第一号通告，日期为1937年2月......日。

由于当局决定裁员，我们筑路苦力中间存在不安情绪。然而，通过俞亚清（Yu Ka Ching）先生给予我们的帮助，我们将不会失业。
工部局已声明并未作出裁员决定，同时公布了以下劳动条件：

“冬季工作时间为每天8½小时，夏季为每天9小时。一等苦力的日薪为0.65元。雨天及节假日，未工作者发给半薪，出勤工作者发给全薪。农历新年放假三天，端午节放假一天；苦力在此期间享受全薪。在这些节假日工作的人将获得双倍工资。”

特此通知苦力们和平工作，不得滋扰。此后，所有苦力应勤勉工作，恪尽职守，不得干扰他人的工作。凡不服从上述指示或从事损害本会声誉的非法活动者，将向工部局报告。

the coolies that Mr. Pardoe of the F.W.D. on the morning of

badges would take place on Saturday, February 27. When
questioned by the coolies concerning the suggestion of
inserting an explanatory announcement in the Chinese press
or of addressing a formal letter to the Coolies Mutual Aid
Society explaining the exchange of working badges, Mr. Pardoe
replied that neither suggestions could be adopted. In
conclusion, the speaker urged the coolies present to give
careful consideration to the matter. Subsequently Chen Kiu-
feng (陳九峰), committee member of the 1st Special District
Citizens' Federation who is the only non-coolie taking an
active interest in the formation of the Coolies' Mutual Aid

Subject P.W.D. Road Construction Coolies of Dixwell Road Depot
- Meeting

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by J. Boyce D.S.I.

At 6 p.m. February 22, 1937, twenty one road
construction coolies claiming to represent coolies attached
to various P.W.D. Depots held a meeting in the Kung Wu
Teashop, 174 Ying Ka Zah Road, Chapei. Li Ching-tsung
(李景春), coolie attached to Dixwell Road Depot,
presided and stated that during an interview on the morning
of February 22, 1937, the P.W.D. authorities explained the
inadvisability of discriminating between road construction
coolies and sewerage coolies in the distribution of work.
The delegation urged to drop any further agitation in
connection with the matter. A general discussion then took
place and it was decided that should the P.W.D. Authorities
insist upon enforcing their new system, they be requested to
adopt the following measures :-

1. That after the exchange of working badges assurance be
given against the discharge of coolies without reason.
2. That badges of different colour be issued so as to
differentiate between those coolies who had been
employed on the permanent staff under the old system,
and those who would be employed together with the old
coolies as casual labourers under the new system.

It was decided to convey these measures to the
P.W.D. Authorities at 10 a.m. February 23.

Subject P.W.D. Authorities interview Road Construction Coolies
of the Central and Northern Districts.
Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by J. Boyu D.S.I.

At about 4.40 p.m. February 22, in the compound of
the Central District Depot, Soochow Road, the P.W.D. authorities
interviewed the road construction coolies of the Central and
Northern Districts, when the revised conditions governing
working hours and pay for holidays were discussed and read
over to them in Chinese. The coolies were told that copies
of these conditions written in Chinese would be posted in
the Depots and godowns. It was also announced that the
numbers of new badges to be issued for the Central District
coolies would be from No.1 to No.250, and those for the
Northern District from No.251 to No.500, while badges from
No.501 to No.750 would be issued to sewage construction coolies.
There would be no change in the working system, with the
exception that the cleaning of drains, which was hitherto
handled by road construction coolies, would in future be done
by sewage coolies. The road construction coolies fearing
that they would not get as much work as usual expressed
dissatisfaction with the latter point. The P.W.D. authorities
then explained to them that if they had any complaints
concerning the new system, their representatives could report
direct to the P.W.D. authorities. The coolies were further
advised not to suspend work in future, because of the loss
which both parties incurred.

During the course of the interview, the coolies
demanded that double pay be issued to them for Christmas and
Foreign New Year Holidays. The P.W.D. authorities promised
to grant them, as an alternative, three days holidays to be
taken by groups in turn; the coolies expressed their
satisfaction with this offer.

制作人：巡官亨奇曼 由副刑事侦缉督察J. Boyu转呈。

1937年2月22日下午4时40分左右，在苏州路中区堆场大院内，工务局当局面谈了中区和北区的筑路苦力，讨论并向他们宣读了经修订的关于工作时间和节假日薪酬的规定（中文）。当局告知苦力，这些规定的中文副本将张贴在各堆场和仓库。此外还宣布，中区苦力的新证件编号将从第1号至第250号，北区苦力从第251号至第500号，而第501号至第750号的证件将发给清沟筑路苦力。工作制度除一点外没有变化，即此前由筑路苦力负责的排水沟清理工作，今后将由清沟苦力负责。筑路苦力担心他们无法像往常一样获得足够的工作量，对最后一点表示不满。工务局当局随即向他们解释，如果他们对新制度有任何投诉，他们的代表可以直接向工务局当局报告。当局还劝告苦力今后不要停工，因为这会给双方造成损失。

在面谈过程中，苦力要求圣诞节和外国新年假期发放双倍工资。工务局当局承诺作为替代方案，给予三天假期，由各组轮流休假；苦力们对这一提议表示满意。

Subject...Unrest among road construction coolies at Maxwell Road Depot

Made by A/C.D.I. Sih tse-liang Forwarded by J. Boyne D.S.I

At 3.05 p.m. February 17, 1937, while six casual coolies attached to the Maxwell Road Depot were attending to sewerage cleaning work at Pingliang Road near Dalny Road, three male Chinese riding bicycles approached them and warned them to cease work as they desired to take over the work themselves. The three intimidators subsequently rode away, while the casual coolies continued their work without further interference.

Enquiries among the coolies show that the three intimidators are believed to be road construction coolies now assigned to the Northern Area and attached to the Maxwell Road Depot, and that the cause of the intimidation was due to opposition to the engagement of casual coolies on sewerage cleaning work, which, as a rule, is undertaken by road construction coolies.

It is learnt that in December, 1936 following the decision of the P.W.D. authorities to reduce the highway staff and re-allocate the working area, the Mwo Road and Dawgin Road Depots were abolished and the 220 and 110 permanent road construction coolies attached to these depots were transferred to the Maxwell Road Sewerage Depot. The latter originally employed on its staff a number of casual coolies who undertook sewerage work. In consequence of the new arrangement, the number of casual coolies was reduced to 35, and following the transfer of the road construction coolies from Mwo Road and Dawgin Road Depots, the Maxwell Road Sewerage Depot, was renamed Maxwell Road Depot. These changes took place on December 16, 1936.

Since the beginning of this year, casual coolies, having no regular sewerage job, were given sewerage cleaning work to perform, this work as a rule, is undertaken by road construction coolies. The assignment of this type of labour to casual

1937年2月17日下午3时05分，当隶属于麦克斯韦路堆栈的六名临时苦力在大连路附近的平凉路进行下水道清洁工作时，三名骑自行车的中国男子接近他们，警告他们停止工作，因为他们希望自己接手这项工作。这三名恐吓者随后骑车离开，而临时苦力则继续工作，未再受到干扰。

At 3.30 p.m. February 16, Mr. Wang Chia Zu
(王家柱), a member of the Investigation Department (调查股)
of the local Tangpu, called at this office and produced a petition
signed by four road construction coolies and stamped by 51 other
coolies of the P.W.D. requesting permission for the formation
and registration of an Association to be called "The Mutual
Aid Association of the P.W.D. Coolies of the International
Settlement."

Mr. Wong asked for the views of the Council on
the subject before the Tangpu gave the necessary permission.
In reply, I stated that I would forward a report to my superiors
for instructions.

In an interview with Mr. Tsu Hsueh Van, the head
of the local General Labour Union, this morning, I impressed
upon him that there was no necessity for workmen connected
with public utilities to form a union; that the application
was signed by a small percentage of the workers and is only
the work of certain agitators, who desire to make use of such
a union to their profit.

Mr. Tsu replied that should the S.M.C. consider
such organization undesirable, he would arrange with the
Tangpu to reject the application.

Date February 16, 1937.

Subject Press report concerning P.W.D. coolies - denial by P.W.D. authorities.

Made by D.P.S. Henchman Forwarded by J. Payne D.S.S.

At 9 a.m. February 15, 1937, Mr. Pardoe, Highway
Engineer of the P.W.D. summoned ten representatives of coolies
from both the Central and Northern Districts to his office in
the Administration Building and explained that there was no
truth in the press report alleging that the new system of
drawing lots in order to decide who should be employed, would
be brought into operation on February 28, 1937. Should there
be an increase in the amount of work to be done, he continued,
extra workers would be employed, and if there should be a
decrease, coolies already in the employment of the P.W.D. would
be chosen by ballot or the choice left to the coolies themselves.
The delegation subsequently withdrew.

At 6.30 p.m. February 15, six foremen of road
construction coolies of various P.W.D. depots held a conference
at the S.M.C. employees' Club, Continental Emporium Building,
and discussed the press report which alleged that the foremen
had deducted coolies' wages during holiday periods. It was
decided to request the P.W.D. authorities to investigate the
matter and to publish a correction in the press.

D.P.S. Henchman

February 15, 1937.    3    Morning Translation.

National Herald and other local newspapers .-

THE S.M.C. AND ITS ROAD WORKERS

The Shanghai Municipal Council had originally
1,400 road workers. The newspaper report that the Council
has 1,200 road workers is incorrect because the S.M.C. had
already dismissed some 40 foremen unconditionally on
January 2. These dismissed foremen were not given any
retirement gratuity or pension.
The road workers have to work 12 hours a day
and are paid only 70¢ per diem.
The S.M.C. has now fixed February 28 as the
date for the drawing of lots to decide which road workers
are to be discharged. The workers will probably organize
some movement when the time arrives.

Coolies Send Letter to S.M.C.

The International Settlement Road Coolies'
Mutual Aid Association yesterday sent the following letter
to the Shanghai Municipal Council:-
"The notification issued by the Council some
time ago stating that a majority of the road coolies will
be discharged created great anxiety among the road workers.
When Hsu Mei Sung (徐美松), a foreman of the Soochow Road
District, held back three days' wages of the coolies and
dismissed fifty coolies, all coolies went on strike.
"Afterwards, the Council gave an assurance that
it would not discharge the coolies. Mr. Yu Ya Ching, one of
the Chinese Councillors, personally told the coolies'
representatives that the Council had made no decision
regarding the discharge of road coolies, but that it
intended, owing to financial stingency, to assign work to the
coolies by the drawing of lots. If the coolies opposed
this measure, work would be distributed among the coolies
without drawing of lots, and the Council would refrain from
engaging any new coolies until all the old hands had been
given work. If any new coolies were employed, they would be
discharged the moment that the work required a smaller
number of coolies. Relief measures would be devised
regarding work on days of rain or snow. Sewerage coolies
and road coolies must not interfere with each other, but
confine themselves to their respective duties. Should a
foreman show favour to any one side and tries to take away
by force the badge issued to a road coolie, a complaint
should be made. As a further means to prevent malpractices
by the foremen, numbered caps would be issued to the coolies.
"Upon receiving this assurance, the road coolies
resumed work.
"Hsu Mei Sung, however, cannot evade responsi-
bility for the strike. Seven years ago, Hsu was a
mechanic. He made a fortune by undertaking sewerage work.
When the sewerage work was completed, he obtained a position
as foreman in the Public Works Department. In order to
give work to the several thousand workers formerly employed
by him, he persuaded the authorities to discharge the road
coolies. He has also been oppressing road coolies. All
page_data.zh:
1937年2月15日。 3 晨间译件。

《国民新闻报》及其他本地报纸 .-

工部局及其道路工人

上海公共租界工部局原本拥有
1,400名道路工人。报纸报道说工部局
有1,200名道路工人，这是不正确的，因为工部局
已于1月2日无条件解雇了约40名领班。这些被解雇的领班
未获得任何退休酬金或养老金。
道路工人每天必须工作12小时
日薪仅为70美分。
工部局现已将2月28日定为
抽签决定哪些道路工人将被解雇的日期。届时工人们可能会组织
某种行动。

苦力致信工部局

国际租界道路苦力互助会昨日向
上海公共租界工部局发出如下信件：-
“工部局前此发布的通告称，大多数道路苦力将
被解雇，这在道路工人中引起了极大的焦虑。
当苏州路区领班徐美松（Hsu Mei Sung）扣留苦力三天工资并
解雇五十名苦力时，所有苦力均罢工。
“随后，工部局保证不会解雇苦力。华董
虞洽卿先生亲自告知苦力代表，工部局并未就
解雇道路苦力一事作出决定，但因财政拮据，
打算通过抽签方式为苦力分配工作。如果苦力反对
这一措施，将在不抽签的情况下在苦力中分配
工作，且在所有老员工都得到工作安排之前，工部局将不再
雇佣新苦力。如果雇佣了新苦力，一旦工作所需
苦力人数减少，他们将立即被解雇。针对雨雪天
的工作，将制定救济措施。下水道苦力
和道路苦力不得相互干扰，而应
恪守各自职责。如果领班偏袒任何一方并试图强行
夺走发给道路苦力的徽章，应提出投诉。作为防止
领班舞弊的进一步手段，将向苦力发放编号帽。
“收到这一保证后，道路苦力
恢复了工作。
“然而，徐美松无法逃避对此次罢工的责
任。七年前，徐是一名机械师。他通过承包下水道工程
发了财。下水道工程完工后，他在工务处
获得了领班的职位。为了给以前受雇于他的数千名工人
提供工作，他说服当局解雇道路
苦力。他还一直压迫道路苦力。所有

page_data.en:
the coolies in other districts were paid wages for the
three days' holiday at the solar New Year, but the workers
of the Soochow Road District did not receive any pay for the
money was misappropriated by Hsu Mei Sung.
"Recently, Hsu Mei Sung attempted to force
the road coolies to change their badges for new ones so that
he could mix his own men with the coolies. When the coolies
refused to give up their badges, Hsi Mei Sung issued new
badges to double the number of the original road coolies.
The badges issued to sewerage coolies, road coolies,
permanent and temporary workers are of the same shape. His
intentions are obvious.
"Thus, the road coolies could no longer be
distinguished from the sewerage coolies, and the road
coolies will not be in a position to argue should they be
discharged as sewerage coolies. All the present road
coolies are thus in danger of being discharged.
"For the sake of peace and order of the
community, and the livelihood of road coolies, we request
you (1) to detail an official to make an investigation;
(2) to issue the wages for the three days' holiday at the
solar New Year to the road coolies of the Soochow Road
District; (3) to dismiss Hsu Mei Sung.
"We advise the Council not to change the
badges as this would give rise to confusion and trouble, but
should the Council deem this inadvisable, we suggest that
different badges be issued to different groups of workers
so that they may be distinguished one from another. We
also request you to issue numbered caps to the coolies in
order to prevent false reports being made regarding the
number of coolies."
page_data.zh:
其他地区的苦力都领取了阳历新年三天假期的工资，但苏州路区的工人
没有收到任何工资，因为钱被徐美松挪用了。
“最近，徐美松试图强迫道路苦力更换新徽章，以便
他可以将自己的人手混入苦力之中。当苦力拒绝
交出徽章时，徐美松发放的新徽章数量是原有道路苦力
数量的两倍。发给下水道苦力、道路苦力、
长期工和临时工的徽章形状相同。其意图
显而易见。
“因此，道路苦力再也无法与下水道苦力
区分开来，如果道路苦力被当作下水道苦力解雇，他们将
处于无法争辩的境地。因此，目前所有的道路
苦力都面临被解雇的危险。
“为了社区的和平与秩序，以及道路苦力的
生计，我们请求你们（1）派遣官员进行调查；
（2）向苏州路区的道路苦力发放阳历新年三天假期的工资；
（3）解雇徐美松。
“我们建议工部局不要更换徽章，因为这会引起
混乱和麻烦，但如果工部局认为此举不可取，我们建议
向不同群体的工人发放不同的徽章，以便
相互区分。我们还请求你们向苦力发放编号帽，
以防止关于苦力人数的虚假报告。”

Subject Activities of P.W.D. road construction coolies.
Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by J. Bayne. D.S.I.

The strike of the 1,500 P.W.D. road construction
coolies, which commenced on January 30, 1937, was called off
during the evening of February 2, and all coolies resumed
work at 6.30 a.m. this morning, February 3, 1937. Fifty coolies
of the Soochow Road Depot, whose badges were withdrawn by the
P.W.D. authorities in January, 1937, were also reinstated,
being issued with badges, and accorded the same treatment as
the others.

The resumption of work was the result of a discussion
on the new system governing the engagement of coolies by the
P.W.D. between Mr. Yu Ya-Ching and Mr. Yei Ngoh-Su, Chinese
members of the S.M.C. and a delegation of five coolies
accompanied by Chen Hiu-Feng (陳九峯), Committee member
of the 1st Special District Citizens' Federation, at 4.45 p.m.
February 2 in the office of the San Peh Steamship Company, 93
Canton Road. During the discussion, Mr. Yu Ya-Ching reiterated
the statement made by the P.W.D. authorities to the foremen on
February 1, which embodied the following three points :-
1) That wages would be paid for working days only.
2) That selection of coolies would be by ballot instead of by
personal choice by foremen as hitherto.
3) That as there is sufficient work on hand, the number of
coolies would not be reduced during the coming few months.

After some discussion, the delegation accepted the
first two conditions and requested that the proposed ballot
system be cancelled and that coolies be given liberty to
arrange among themselves to work on alternate shifts. In
addition they also requested Mr. Yu Ya-Ching and Mr. Yei Ngoh-Su
to negotiate with the P.W.D. authorities on the following :-

Five representatives of the coolies named Li Ching-
tsung (李景春) (coolie No.45), Liu Hwan-yung (劉煥文)
(Coolie No.200), Kwan Bu-yuin (關步瀛) (Coolie No.195),
Tsei Fu-yung (蔡富榮) (Coolie No.57) and Wong Shang-zai
(王双才) (Coolie No.296) called at the San Peh Steamship
Company, 93 Canton Road, at 4.45 p.m. February 1, 1937, and
interviewed Mr. Yu Ya-ching who asked them to call again at
yet
5 p.m. February 2, 1937, as he had not/discussed the question
with other Chinese members of the Council.

At 7.30 a.m. February 2, 1937, seven representatives
of the road construction coolies of the P.W.D. Soochow Road
Depot, called at the Depot and interviewed the foreigner in
charge who, through the interpretation of Chinese foreman
Zee Kei-sung, re-iterated the declaration made by the P.W.D.
authorities to the effect that the only changes in the new
system were :-
a) That wages be issued only for working days.
b) That selection of coolies for work where fewer workers
than available are required will be by ballot instead of
individual choice by foreman.

The callers were assured that the S.M.C. would not
dismiss a single worker and were persuaded to instruct all
strikers to resume work immediately. Expressing their
satisfaction with the arrangements, the callers stated that
owing to time required to circulate this information, work
would not be resumed earlier than February 3, 1937. Before
dispersing, the callers were advised to instruct all strikers
not to interfere with coolies who had been sent out to attend
to important work on streets.

In order to avoid interference from the authorities,
the road construction coolies of the P.W.D. depots decided
on January 31, 1937 to send a delegation of 35 persons to
the Shanghai City Government, Civic Centre, for the purpose
of submitting a memorial for assistance in their dispute with
the I.W.D. It was also decided to inform all delegates to
assemble at the I.W.D. No. 1 Shop, Foshan Road
near Boundary Road, Chapei, at 9 a.m. February 1. These
35 delegates arrived at the teashop at 10 a.m. and are now
proceeding to the City Government by motor truck, in company
with Chen Jiu-foon (陈九峰), committee member of the 1st
Special District Citizens' Federation, who has been assisting
the coolies.

At about 7 p.m. February 1, 1937, some 100 strikers
gathered on Nanking Road near the Settlement boundary, with
the intention of proceeding to the Civic Centre. Eventually,
they decided to appoint five delegates to call at the City
Government, whilst the others should disperse and re-assemble
at the same place at 5 p.m. to-day, or 6 a.m. February 2 in
order to hear the result of the appeal. During the general
discussion copies of a printed handbill entitled "A Manifesto
issued by the Road Construction Coolies' Mutual Aid Society"
were distributed among the coolies by their representative
named Wong Lih-sung (王立生). (Translation of this handbill
is attached to Special Branch Report dated January 28, 1937).

instruction received by them on the morning of January 30
but quietly dispersed owing to the presence of the Municipal

At 10 a.m. February 1, 1937, thirty five Chinese coolies
claiming to represent strikers of various F.W.D. depots, who had
assembled at the Hwa Yang Pao Shing Lur Teashop, 7 Raoshan Road,
left by motortruck for the Civic Centre. Chen Kiu-feng (陳九峯),

who has been assisting the coolies in the strike movement,
accompanied the delegation.

When the truck arrived at Si Yueh Wei Road, it was stopped
by the Chinese Police who told the delegation they could proceed
no further. After some argument, it was arranged that fifteen
delegates be permitted to continue the journey. The delegation
interviewed one named Wong Ping (王冰), a staff member of
the Bureau of Social Affairs, who, after receiving their petition,

当卡车到达四悦威路（音译：Si Yueh Wei Road）时，被中国警察拦下，警察告诉代表团他们不能再继续前进。经过一番争论，商定允许十五名代表继续行程。代表团会见了一名在社会局任职的名叫王冰（王冰）的人员，他在收到请愿书后，建议他们不要进行任何非法活动，因为工部局是一个行政机构，并应耐心等待虞洽卿先生谈判的结果，随后他们便离开了。

代表团随后前往当地党部，一名在民众训练部任职的名叫樊国成（樊國成）的人员会见了他们，并指示他们通知所有罢工者在党部调查期间保持和平与秩序。随后，众人集体返回位于云南路丙子社（Ping Tsz Club）3号的互助社临时办事处，在那里陈九峰建议代表们于下午4时回到该社，以便集体前往广东路93号的三德轮船公司办公室，听取虞洽卿先生的谈判结果。在解散之前，陈和代表们主张，如果虞洽卿先生关于调解的答复证明不能令人满意，则应尝试

Subject P.W.D. Road Construction coolies - activities.

Made by D.I. Sih Tse Liang Forwarded by J. Layne C.S.I.

At 12.25 p.m. January 30, some thirty Chinese claiming
to represent F.W.D. Road Construction coolies of various depots,
who are on strike, proceeded in small groups to the Administration
building, S.M.C. Three of the delegates named Liu nwan wen
(刘焕文), Li Ching Tsung (李景春) and Tsai roo yung (蔡雷荣)
interviewed Mr. T. K. Ho, Chinese Assistant Secretary, and
submitted a petition for the cancellation of the decision of
the P.W.D. regarding the new system of engaging coolies. In
reply Mr. Ho promised to refer their petition to the Council,
whereupon the delegates withdrew.

These representatives subsequently called upon Mr. Yu
Yah Ching (虞洽卿), Chinese member of the S.M.C. at his office
in the San Peh Steamship Co., 93 Canton Road, and made a similar
appeal. They were advised to return at 5 p.m. February 1, 1937.

A subsequent visit by these delegates to the Chinese
Ratepayers' Association resulted in a promise by the Secretary
of the Association that the matter would be taken up with the
S.M.C..

It is learned that some 70 delegates of these coolies will
proceed on the morning of February 1, 1937 to the Shanghai City
Government, the Bureau of Social Affairs and the local Tangpu
to appeal for assistance. The number of appelants may be greater
as some of the coolies may participate in the visit of their own
accord. No definite plan has been formed as to how to proceed to
the City Government. The coolies will assemble at various places
along the Settlement boundary in the Eastern District.

1月30日下午12时25分，约三十名自称代表各堆栈罢工之工务局筑路苦力的华人，分批前往工部局行政大楼。三名名为刘焕文 (Liu nwan wen)、李景春 (Li Ching Tsung) 和蔡雷荣 (Tsai roo yung) 的代表会见了华籍助理秘书何德奎 (T. K. Ho) 先生，并提交请愿书，要求撤销工务局关于雇佣苦力新制度的决定。作为答复，何先生承诺将他们的请愿书转呈董事会，随后代表们离去。

这些代表随后前往广东路93号三北轮船公司办公室，拜访了工部局华董虞洽卿 (Yu Yah Ching) 先生，并提出了类似的请求。他们被告知于1937年2月1日下午5时返回。

这些代表随后拜访华人纳税会，该会秘书承诺会将此事向工部局提出。

据悉，约70名苦力代表将于1937年2月1日上午前往上海市政府、社会局及当地党部请求援助。申诉人数可能更多，因为部分苦力可能会自发参与此次行动。目前尚未制定前往市政府的具体计划。苦力们将在东区租界边界沿线的各处集合。

Date January 30, 1937.

Subject Unrest among I.W.D. Road Construction Coolies.

Made by L.I. Sih Tee-liang Forwarded by [Signature]

One of the causes of unrest among I.W.D. road
construction coolies over the introduction of a new system
is reported to be that a number of the permanent coolies
at present employed at various depots have obtained their
working number-badges by payment.

There are certain loafers who, it is reported,
ally with the senior staff and obtain working number-badges
in the loafers name. After working for some time, he sells
it to any person who desires a job but has no way to obtain
one. The price of the badge varies from $80.00 to $120.00
each. After selling his badge, the loafer will arrange with
his old acquaintance to obtain another one which he will again
sell later on. It is reported that a number of coolies
now holding number-badges have been the victims of this
malpractice.

Consequently, when the new system is introduced
these coolies will suffer an irrevocable loss, and as they
have no other way to obtain redress, there is every
possibility that they will enforce their opposition by
intimidating new coolies selected.

[Signature]

日期：1937年1月30日。

事由：工务局筑路苦力中的不安情绪。

制作：督察 Sih Tee-liang 转呈：[签名]

据报道，工务局筑路苦力因引入新制度而产生不安情绪的原因之一是，目前受雇于各堆栈的部分长期苦力是通过付款获得其工作号牌（badge）的。

据报道，有一些游手好闲之徒与高级职员勾结，以这些闲散人员的名义获取工作号牌。工作一段时间后，他将其出售给任何想要工作但无法通过正常途径获得工作的人。每个号牌的价格在80.00元至120.00元之间。卖出号牌后，该闲散人员会与旧识安排再获取一个号牌，以便日后再次出售。据报道，目前持有号牌的一些苦力已成为这种舞弊行为的受害者。

因此，当新制度实施时，这些苦力将遭受不可挽回的损失，且由于他们别无他法寻求补救，极有可能通过恐吓新选定的苦力来强行表达反对意见。

[签名]

page_data.en:
APPENDIX "A"

Translation

We have been in the employ of the Shanghai Municipal
Council as road building coolies for many years. The
prosperity Shanghai enjoys at present is traceable to our
efforts in building roads. It is a surprise to us that
we are all dismissed. Recalling the past efforts we have
exerted and anticipating what will be in store for us in
future only increases our resentment. Since the Shanghai
Municipal Council has turned a deaf ear to our request for
reinstatement, we are compelled to form a strong organization
with a view to opposing determinedly the Council's oppression.
We hope that assistance will be rendered to us by the public
in order that we may not be homeless.

According to the Shanghai Municipal Council, the
discharge of the road coolies is to curtail expenses of the
Council, but as a matter of fact, the wages of the road
coolies numbering more than one thousand amount to no more
than the salaries of ten of the Council's senior foreign
employees. If the Council is sincere in its intention to
carry out a retrenchment policy, the big salaries of its
senior foreign employees should be reduced. There is no
necessity of dismissing more than one thousand road coolies,
whose unemployment will only increase the social unrest
prevailing at present.

Concerning the road work, since more roads are built
and widened and more vehicles are put into operation, more
road coolies should be employed instead of reduced. This is
the second point that the dismissal of the road coolies is
unreasonable.

Employees in various trades have demanded increases
in wages during the past several years, but we have not
submitted any demand for an increase. The dismissal of the
page_data.zh:
附录 “A”

译文

我们受雇于上海公共租界工部局担任筑路苦力已有多年。上海目前的繁荣可追溯至我们修筑道路的努力。令我们惊讶的是，我们全部被解雇了。回想过去我们所付出的努力，并预见未来的遭遇，只会增加我们的愤慨。既然上海公共租界工部局对我们的复职请求充耳不闻，我们被迫组成一个强有力的组织，以坚决反对理事会的压迫。我们希望公众能向我们提供援助，以免我们流离失所。

据上海公共租界工部局称，解雇筑路苦力是为了削减理事会的开支，但事实上，一千多名筑路苦力的工资总额不超过理事会十名外籍高级职员的薪水。如果理事会真诚打算执行紧缩政策，应降低其外籍高级职员的高薪。没有必要解雇一千多名筑路苦力，他们的失业只会加剧目前普遍存在的社会动荡。

关于道路工程，既然修建和拓宽的道路越来越多，投入运营的车辆也越来越多，理应雇佣更多的筑路苦力，而不是减少。这是解雇筑路苦力不合理的第二点。

过去几年，各行各业的雇员都要求增加工资，但我们从未提出过加薪要求。解雇

page_data.en:
-2-
loyal road coolies shows another aspect of the unreasonableness
on the part of the Council.
During the January 28 incident, all the defence
works were erected by the road coolies, who accomplished
the assignments in the midst of gunfire. A number of the
road coolies were injured and killed in line of duty. It
is unreasonable as well as callous on the part of the Council
to dismiss those faithful and meritorious road coolies.
In a word, the dismissal of the road coolies by the
Council is absolutely unreasonable and is an act of contempt
for the Chinese. When the Council requires our services,
it calls us in and when our services are not needed, we are
dismissed without considering the meritorious services we
have rendered. The Council thinks that the road coolies
will submit to its decision, but we will not submit to the
dismissal to the detriment of the dignity of the country.
We will oppose the decision until a satisfactory settlement
is reached.
page_data.zh:
-2-
忠诚的筑路苦力一事，显示出工部局理事会的另一面无理之处。
在一·二八事变期间，所有防御工事均由筑路苦力修筑，他们在枪林弹雨中完成了任务。多名筑路苦力在执勤中受伤或牺牲。理事会解雇这些忠诚且有功的筑路苦力，既不合理，亦显冷漠。
总之，理事会解雇筑路苦力之举绝对无理，是对中国人的蔑视。当理事会需要我们的服务时，便征召我们；当不再需要我们的服务时，便将我们解雇，而不顾我们所作出的贡献。理事会以为筑路苦力会顺从其决定，但我们不会接受这种有损国家尊严的解雇。我们将反对该决定，直至达成令人满意的解决为止。

Date. January 27, 1937.

Subject Unrest among F.M.D. Road Coolies.

Made by. D. I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by. Gilmore DI

（批：W. Hughes
wtf & plus
at 11.50am.
Dix）

Chen Kiu-feng (陳九峰), Committee member of the
1st S.M.D. District Citizens' Federation is arranging to hold
a meeting of delegates of the road coolies of various S.M.D.
Depots at 5 p.m. to-day, January 27 in the office of
the Association in the Chinese Chamber of Commerce building,
North Soochow Road. The discussion at this meeting will,
it is believed, be confined to the following, which has been
prepared by Chen Kiu-feng:-

1) That a society entitled "The Shanghai Municipality Interna-
tional Settlement Road Construction Coolies Mutual Aid
Society" (上海市公共租界築路苦力互助會) be formed.

2) That a manifesto be issued to acquaint the public with the
decision of the S.M.C. to expel Chinese coolies in the name
of retrenchment and that appeals be made to the local
Chinese authorities and public bodies.

（批：C.P. Aida）

3) That ten delegates of coolies be elected as members
of the committee of the Society.

4) That in opposing the decision of the S.M.C. to reduce the
number of coolies, the following measures be adopted :-
a) That the S.M.C. be urged to cancel its decision.
b) That all coolies retain their employment pending a
settlement of the dispute.
c) That should any coolie be actually dismissed, a general
strike be declared.

（印：OFFICE OF COMMISSIONER OF POLICE 1113）

Simultaneously, Chen Kiu-feng has approached Chinese
newsreporters of local news agencies to render assistance in
the matter by conducting propaganda in favour of the coolies
through the medium of the press. The propaganda, Chen has
explained, should contain the following points:-

日期：1937年1月27日。

主题：工部局道路苦力中的动荡情况。

呈报人：督察 施子良（Sih Tse-liang） 转呈人：吉尔莫尔（Gilmore）督察

（批注：W. Hughes
wtf & plus
上午11时50分。
Dix）

上海市公共租界第一区市民联合会委员陈九峰（Chen Kiu-feng）正安排于今日（1月27日）下午5时，在北苏州路中国商会大楼内的该会办公室，召开来自工部局各堆栈的道路苦力代表会议。据信，此次会议的讨论将限于由陈九峰拟定的以下事项：

1) 成立一个名为“上海市公共租界筑路苦力互助会”的社团。

2) 发表宣言，向公众告知工部局以裁员为名驱逐中国苦力的决定，并向中国地方当局及公共团体发出呼吁。

（批注：C.P. Aida）

3) 选举十名苦力代表担任该会委员会委员。

4) 为反对工部局削减苦力人数的决定，采取以下措施：
a) 敦促工部局撤销其决定。
b) 在争议解决之前，所有苦力保留其工作。
c) 若有任何苦力被实际解雇，则宣布总罢工。

（印章：警务处处长办公室 1113）

与此同时，陈九峰已接触本地新闻机构的中文记者，请求他们通过媒体进行宣传以支持苦力，从而在此事上提供协助。陈解释说，宣传内容应包含以下几点：

（批注：S.I.
D&R
27/1）

1) The policy of retrenchment should confine itself to highly
paid staff.
2) The economic depression in Shanghai is due to the increase
in the number of unemployed.
3) Widening and extension of streets increases the work of the
coolies and requires more men.
4) Increase in the traffic damages the road surface.
5) The merits of the coolies during the past years should not be
overlooked.
6) While workers of other trades all receive an increase in
wages, road coolies only desire to retain their job.
It is learned that a movement is afoot among the road
coolies to collect 50 cents from each worker for the purpose of
raising a fund to defray the expenses incurred in furtherance
of their opposition to the S.M.C.
As far as can be ascertained, Chen's office in the
1st Special District Citizens' Federation, Chinese Chamber of
Commerce building, North Soochow Road, as well as the Ping Tsz
Club (平 3 □), 3 Dz Dzoh Li, Yunnan Road (Louza District),
are used as the main communication addresses between Chen and
the coolies, while the latter are, as their customary rule,
using various small teashops and hot water shops on Amoy and
Urga Roads and vicinity as meeting places.

1) 裁员政策应仅限于高薪职员。
2) 上海的经济萧条是由于失业人数增加所致。
3) 街道的拓宽与延伸增加了苦力的工作量，因而需要更多的人手。
4) 交通量的增加损坏了路面。
5) 不应忽视过去几年中苦力的功绩。
6) 虽然其他行业的工人都获得了加薪，但道路苦力只希望保住工作。
据悉，道路苦力中正酝酿一场运动，向每名工人收取50分，旨在筹集资金，以支付他们反对工部局（S.M.C.）所产生的费用。
据查，陈氏在苏州河北路中国商会大楼内的第一特区市民联合会办事处，以及位于劳勃生路（Louza District）云南路德德里3号（3 Dz Dzoh Li, Yunnan Road）的平社俱乐部（Ping Tsz Club (平 3 □)），被用作陈氏与苦力之间的主要联络地址；而苦力们则按惯例，利用厦门路和乌尔加路及其附近的各种小茶馆和热水店作为集会场所。

Made by D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by [Signature]

At 11 a.m. January 25, 1937, ten Chinese claiming
to represent F.W.D. road coolies of various depots called
at the 1st Special District Citizens' Federation, Chinese
Chamber of Commerce building, North Soochow Road, and
submitted a petition for assistance in opposing the decision
of the S.M.C. to reduce the number of permanent coolies.
These coolies were received by Chen Kiu-feng (陈九峰),
committee member of the Federation, who promised to refer
their request to a committee meeting which would be held on
January 27, and asked them to return at 3 p.m. January 27
for a reply. These coolies subsequently made a similar
appeal to the Chinese Ratepayers' Association, 59 Hongkong
Road, where Dau Loh-jing (陶露勤), Secretary of the
Association interviewed them and promised support of their
petition. The callers withdrew at 12.15 p.m.

Petition for Relief for S.M.C. Road Coolies

We have been in the employ of the S.M.C.
as road coolies for a period of from ten to twenty
years. We have been carrying out our duties
diligently in all kinds of weather and in some
cases of loyalty to duty some have even sacrificed
their lives. With the meagre wages we are barely
able to support our families. We are really living
from hand to mouth.

To carry out a retrenchment policy, the S.M.C.
has decided to dispense with the services of 90% of
the road coolies at the end of January.

When we heard of the intention of the S.M.C.,
we all became much alarmed. When the Settlement was
first established with spaces here and there, the.
Council employed more than one thousand coolies to
clean the streets, and a large number of casual
workers in case of need. During the past several
years, the number of roads has been increased and
their surfaces have been widened. The number of
vehicles has also been increasing. In consequence
of these factors, more road coolies should be employed
instead of discharged. It is callousness on the part
of the S.M.C. to discharge a large number of the road
coolies on the ground of the present business depression.

The enforcement of the retrenchment policy in
our direction will not only throw us out of employment
but deprive our dependants of the means of subsistence.
We have been loyal to our duties and have done nothing
against the law. To discharge us is contrary to the
International Labor Law.

译文
上海公共租界工部局道路苦力请求救济书

我们受雇于上海公共租界工部局，担任道路苦力已十年至二十年不等。无论何种天气，我们始终勤勉履职，其中一些人甚至因忠于职守而牺牲了生命。凭借微薄的工资，我们仅能勉强维持家计，实乃朝不保夕。

为执行紧缩政策，上海公共租界工部局决定于一月底裁撤百分之九十的道路苦力。

闻悉工部局之意图，我等无不深感惊恐。租界初建之时，地段尚属零星，工部局即雇用千余名苦力清扫街道，并备有大量临时工以备不时之需。过去数年间，道路数量增加，路面亦加宽阔。车辆数目也在不断增多。鉴于这些因素，本应增聘而非裁减道路苦力。工部局以当前商业萧条为由，裁撤大量道路苦力，实属冷漠无情。

若对我等执行紧缩政策，不仅将使我们失业，更将剥夺我们所扶养家属的生计来源。我们一直忠于职守，从未有任何违法之举。裁撤我们违背国际劳工法。

Sir.

This Department has been instructed by the Council to economise in all possible ways. All salaries have been reduced. Economy in labour is also to be effected.

Gangers and Grade I Coolies.

On and after January 30th. 1937. until further notice in all districts, except Rubicon Sub-district. Gangers and Grade I coolies only will be employed. These gangers and coolies will be paid weekly. as at present. but. with the exception of special duty men will receive pay only for the time during which they actually work and will be subject to daily engagement and discharge as circumstances may require. The rates of pay will be as at present that is:-

Gangers 0.79 per day
Grade I Coolies 0.65 " "

Rubicon Sub-District

In Rubicon Sub-district. in addition to Gangers and Grade I coolies Grade II and III coolies will also be employed. All coolies will be paid in the manner laid down for gangers and Grade I coolies and will receive the same daily pay as at present that is:-

Gangers 0.79 per day

先生：

本处奉工部局指示，须尽一切可能厉行节约。所有薪金均已削减。亦须在劳工方面实行节约。

工头及一级苦力。

自1937年1月30日起，直至另行通知为止，除鲁比孔分区外，各区仅雇用工头及一级苦力。这些工头和苦力将如目前一样按周支薪，但除特别勤务人员外，仅就其实际工作时间支付薪水，并视情况需要按日雇用或解雇。薪资率维持现状，即：-

工头 每日0.79元
一级苦力 每日0.65元

鲁比孔分区

在鲁比孔分区，除工头及一级苦力外，还将雇用二级和三级苦力。所有苦力均将按照针对工头和一级苦力规定的方式支付薪水，并领取与目前相同的日薪，即：-

工头 每日0.79元
一级苦力 每日0.65元
二级 " 每日0.57元
三级 " 每日0.49元

劳工甄选。

所需苦力将于发薪日前一天（星期日除外）通过抽签方式选定。若在一周内的任何一天认为有必要增加或减少苦力人数，则将被雇用或解雇的人员将

supervised by the Chief Inspector in charge of the Area concerned
and the Inspector in charge of labour in the depot concerned.
Special Duty Men.
Not more than 50 men in each area will be selected
by merit from artisans and Grade I coolies for special duty work
and these men will be employed on a permanent weekly basis. These
will be trained men who show ability in their work. They will be
selected by the Assistant Engineer and Chief Inspector of the Area
concerned.

---------------------

In their own interests, coolies are warned that the
payment of gratuities directly or indirectly to Foremen or any
other employees of the Council is unnecessary and prohibited.
Offenders will be dismissed.

W A T Sanders.
Highways Engineer.

Draft ef an agreement between the road construction 
foremen (Brass and Iron badges) and coolies of the 
International Public Works Department. 


Because we, doth foremen and coolies, are of the 
labour class and have close working relations, we should aid 
each other so that we will both live in prosperity. With 
thin aim in view, we decided to organize a mtual aid society 
to promote our welfare. Hereafter both foremen and coolies 
will maintain a united front. 

The following terms are agreed upon by representatives 
of both sides; any one side or individual who fails to observe 
this agreement will be dealt with by the Society. 


Arte 1. During working hours, coolies should follow the 
directions of the foremen, while the latter should 
behave properly towards the coolies. Bach should 
do his duty diligently. 


Art. 2. After working hours, both foremen and coolies enjoy 
equality, no jealousy should exist between then. 


Aart. 3. When a coolie is lazy or behaves badly, the foreman 
should not report it to his senior, but should note 
the number and name of the coolie concerned and 
report to the Society through the representative 
(? of the foremen). The society will give advice 
to the coolies or punish him. 


Art. 4. The coolies should not report to their seniors 
(ranks higher than foreman) any smbesslement, illegal 
act, or other breach of regulations, committed by 
their foremen. 


Art. 5. If foremen are guilty of oppressions, the coolies 
should not oper direct negotiations with their 
foremen but should report the matter to the Society. 
fhe society, on receiving the report, will investigate 
the case and punish, if necessary, the foreman 
concerned. 


Art. 6. If the 8.M.C. authorities oppress the foremen, the 
coolies should efford them, the foremen, their 
wholehearted support. 


art. 7. If the 8.M.C. authorities oppress the coolies, the 
foremen should afford them, the coolies, their 
wholehearted support. 


Art. 8. The coolies and foremen should support each other 
at all times.

13. 


The foremen and coolies should support their 
leader and obey him. 


The foremen and coolies should strictly adhere to 
and support the regulations of the Society. 


The foremen and coclies will reject exploitation 
by any party, or clique. 


Should any one failf to observe this agreeement, 
it will be regarded as a sign that he is willing 
to forfeit his qualifications as a coolie or 
foreman and is willing receive punishment from

The International Settlement Read Coolies' 
Mutual Aid As-ooiation yesterday sent the fcllowing letter 
to the Shanghai Munioipal Counnils- 

“The notification issued by the Council some 
time ago stating that a majority cf the road coolies will 
be discharged create reat anxiety among the road workers. 
When Hau Mei Sung (73 )» a foreman of the Soochow Road 
Distriot, held back’ threé days' wages of the coolies and 
dismissed fifty coolies,alk coolies went on strike. 

Yafterwards, the Council gave an a:surance thit 
it would not disoharge the coolies. Mr. Yu Ya Ching, one of 
the Chinese Councillors, personally told the coolies' 
representatives that the Counoil had made no decia@ion 
regarding the disoharge of road coolies, but that it 
intended,owing to financial stingenoy,to assign work to the 
coolies by the drawing of lote. If the coolies opposed 
this measure, work would be distributed among the coolies 
without drewing ef lots, and the Council would refrain from 
engaging any new coolies until all the old hands had been 
@iven work. If any new coolies were employed, they would be 
discharged the moment that the work reguired a senaller 
number of coolies. Relief measures would be devised 
regarding work on days of rain or snow. Sewerage coolies 
and road coolies must not interfere with each other, but 
confine themselves to their respeotive duties. Should a 
foreman show favour to any one side and tries to take away 
by force the badge issued to a road coolie, a complaint 
should be made. As a further means to prevent mabractioes 
by the foremen, numbered Gaps would be issued to the coolies. 

“Upon receiving this assurance, the road coolies 
resumed work. 

“Hau Mei Sung, however, cannot evade responsi- 
bility for the strike. Seven years ago, Hsu was a 
mechanio. He made a fortune by undertaking sewerage work. 
When the sewerage work was completed, he obtained a position 
as foreman in the Public Worka Department. Im order to 
Eive work to the several thousand workers formerly employec 
by him, he persuaded the authorities to discharge the road 
coolies. has also been oppressing road coolics. All 


the coolies in other districts were paid wages for the 

three days' holiday at the solar New Year, but the workers 
of the Soochow Road Distrint did not receive any pay fer the 
money was misappropriated by Hsu Mei Sung. 

“Recently, Hsu Mei Sung attempted to force 
the road ccolies to change their badges for new ones so that 
he could mix his own men with the aoclies. When the coolies 
refused to give up their badges, Hsi Mei Sung issued new 
badges to couble the number of the original road coolies. 
The badges issued to sewerage coosies, road coolies, 
permanent and temporary workers are of the same shapes His 
intentions are obvious. 

“Thus, the road coolies could no longer be 
distinguished from the sewerage ooolies, and the road 
coolies will not be in a position to argue shouid they be 
discharged as sewerage eoolies. All the present road 
ecolies are thus in danger of being discharged. 

“For the eake of pease and order of the 
aommunity, and the livelihood of road coolies, we request 
(1) to detail an official to make an investigation; 

2) to issue the wages for the thre- days' holiday at the 
solar New Year to the road coolies of the Sooch.w Road 
Distriots (3) to dismiss Hou Mei Sung. 

“We advise the Council not to ohange the 
badges as this would give rise to confusion and trouble, but 
should the Council deem this inadvisable, we suggest that 
different badges be issued to different groups of workers 
so that they may be distinguished one from another. We 
also request you to issue numbered oaps tc the coolies in 
order to prevent false reports being made regarding the 
number of coolies."
